caveats: The audiovisual archive has not been fully transcribed or content-reviewed in this bounded pass.
The current absence of posted approved minutes is publication-state evidence, not evidence that the meeting or vote did not occur.
No individual's citizenship or immigration status is inferred or recorded.

conclusions: The September 1 final-record gap is no longer accurately described as 'no native meeting record located'; an official audiovisual record is publicly available.
Approved minutes, roll-call attribution, final enacted text, effective date, and appointment outcomes remain unresolved until the recording is reviewed and/or final municipal records are recovered.
counterarguments: An archive entry is not a substitute for content-level review of the recording.
A media report describing an 18-2 result does not identify the native roll-call record or final codified text.
findings: Danbury's official Granicus archive publicly indexes the September 1, 2026 City Council meeting as a two-hour audiovisual record with Video, MP3, and MP4 access surfaces.
The existence of this native recording materially narrows the evidence gap for agenda item 18 and the four police appointment communications already identified in the canonical September 1 agenda.
Because the recording was not fully reviewed in this pass, the reported 18-2 ordinance outcome and appointment dispositions are not promoted here as facts derived from the video.
unresolved: Review/transcript of the September 1 recording around agenda item 18 and police appointment items.

Final enacted/codified sections 22-19 through 22-30, formal ordinance/resolution identifier, and effective date.

evidence.claim: The official municipal archive exposes a two-hour September 1 City Council meeting recording while the canonical September 1 agenda already identifies the police-ordinance and appointment agenda surfaces that require final disposition review.

summary: The City's official Granicus archive supplies a native audiovisual evidence path for the September 1, 2026 council meeting even though approved minutes are still absent from the Agenda Center. This narrows the remaining #2514 blocker without converting an unreviewed recording into a roll-call or enactment claim.
